title: Carrying Grief Into Training: Reproductive Loss and Counselor Identity Development
abstract: ABSTRACT This preliminary study examined how counselors‐in‐training (CITs) with lived experience of reproductive loss made sense of those experiences in relation to their developing counselor identity and how they described the role of shared grief vocabulary in that sense‐making. Three CITs enrolled in or recently graduated from a CACREP‐accredited program, all members of a voluntary grief exploration student group, completed semi‐structured interviews analyzed using interpretative phenomenological analysis. Three themes were developed, addressing disenfranchised grief and identity disruption, misattuned support, and counselor identity development. Participants described their reproductive grief as a source of clinical attunement and of specific countertransference pulls and described having language for the experience as both personally validating and professionally clarifying. Implications for grief content in counselor preparation and for grief‐attuned supervision are considered within the study's preliminary scope.
